rationale: The audience is individual developers and ML hobbyists — a tech-savvy cohort that skews strongly toward free tools, community wikis, and existing benchmarking sites (like llm.ggerganov.com or everymac.com). While hardware spend is real, software spend on a benchmarking tool is not well evidenced: no paid substitutes at meaningful price points exist, and the HN thread is a question post, not a frustrated-with-a-product post. Buyer clarity is weak because 'developers running local LLMs' spans students, hobbyists, and professionals with very different willingness to pay — no specific budget holder or purchase trigger is named. The deciding factor is low willingness to pay for a tool in a space dominated by open-source and community knowledge.
solution_plan: WHAT: A web-based compatibility checker — enter a model name and MacBook spec (chip, unified memory) and get a predicted run quality score and configuration tips. BUILD: Factory builds a Claude-powered lookup that parses model metadata (parameters, quantization, context length) against Apple Silicon memory bandwidth tables and generates a recommendation; hosted as a static page with a one-time or subscription Stripe link. SELL: Reach HN, r/LocalLLaMA, and r/MachineLearning communities via show-posts and targeted Reddit ads; outreach approved by operator before sending. MAINTAIN: Model database updated via a periodic Claude scrape; support is an FAQ page; billing via Stripe. Only recurring human touch: approving outreach batches. REALITY CHECK: The audience expects this for free — monetization is the hardest unsolved problem here and solo viability is marginal without a clear paid-tier hook.
notes: Does not reach min_total_to_validate threshold of 5.5. Willingness_to_pay at 4 is below build_gate floor of 5; buyer_clarity at 5 is below build_gate floor of 6.
